This appeal coming on for admission this day, th e cour  following:
 ORDER

This Miscellaneous Appeal under Section 173(1) of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is preferred feeling aggrieved by the award dated 26-04-2023 in MACC No. 1923/19 passed by 13th Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Jabalpur for enhancement of Rs. 2 lacs compensation for personal injuries.

entities.text: 13th Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
2. Facts in brief are that the appellant filed an application under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act,
1988 for personal injuries that was caused on 24- 02-2019 at about 7:00 PM by negligent driving of Auto-rickshaw No. MP-34R- 1917 by respondent No.1 and owned by respondent No.2 and insured with respondent No.3-Chola Mandalam Insurance Company Limited near Kalyanpura in the Shri Raghuveer Athya vs Shri Param Singh on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89548896/
1 jurisdiction of police station Damoh Dehat District- Damoh.

entities.text: Shri Raghuveer Athya vs Shri Param Singh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3. A compensation of Rs. 17 lacs was claimed.

It is claimed that he suffered permanent physical disability due to injuries and his age was 32 years and was earning Rs. 9,000/- per month.
4.
Respondent No.3 contested the claim.

The tribunal framed issues and recorded the testimony of appellant- Raghuvir Athya (PW-1) and Ganesh @ Chhotu (PW-2) and the trial Court admitted Ex.
P/1 to Ex. P/39 and defence examined the Clerk of RTO office Damoh Shri Sanjay Rathore as (DW-1), Law Officer of Chola Mandalam Insurance Company- Pawan Kumar Prajapati as (DW_2)
and admitted Ex. D/1 to Ex. D/2.
5.

entities.text: Chola Mandalam Insurance Company- Pawan Kumar Prajapati
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The Tribunal assessed 15% permanent physical disability to the appellant.

In paragraph-18 of the award, tribunal assessed the age of appellant between 31-35 years and income of the appellant as Rs.
7500/- per month and adding the enhancement of 40% as future prospect calculated the total loss of future income as Rs.3,02,400/-, applying the multiplier of 16 awarded a total compensation of Rs. 5,
12,271/- in the following heads :-
 (a) Medical expenses : Rs. 1,86,3  (b) Loss of earning due to : Rs. 3,02,4  permanent physical disability  (c) Loss of income : Rs. 7500/
 (d) Conveyance :
 (e) Attendant charges :
 (f) Special Diet   (g) Pain & sufferings  ------------------------------------------------------------------------
Total = Rs. 5,12,271/-
------------------------------------------------------------------------
6.

This appeal has been preferred feeling aggrieved by award on the ground that the income of the appellant ought to have been assessed as Rs. 9,000/- per month and permanent physical disability ought to have been assessed at 40% and interest of 12% ought to have been awarded.
7. Counsel for the respondent opposed the appeal.
8. Perused the record.

Shri Raghuveer Athya vs Shri Param Singh on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89548896/
2

entities.text: Shri Raghuveer Athya vs Shri Param Singh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 9. Considered the finding of Tribunal regarding admitting the disability certificate Ex. P/38 even without examining the doctor who issued the physical disability certificate and reasons recorded in paragraph-18 of the award for assessing the permanent physical disability of 15% as a whole body for injuries of compound fracture Proximal Humerus, 5th metacarpal right.
The findings of tribunal is proper regarding the percentage of disability.

The tribunal ought to have assessed the income of Rs. 7950/- per month instead of Rs. 7500/- per month and accordingly, the compensation in the heads of loss of future income is enhanced to Rs. 18,144/-.

In the head of pain and sufferings, it is enhanced to Rs. 20,000/- and in head of attendant, it is enhanced to Rs. 7,000/-, in the head of special diet, it is enhanced to Rs. 7,000/- and in the head of loss of income during treatment, it is enhanced by Rs. 16,350/-.

10. This appeal is partly allowed and a compensation of Rs. 68,494/-( Rupees Sixty Eight Thousand Four Hundred Ninety Four) is enhanced with interest @ 6% per month from the date of application i.e.15-05-2019.

(GAJENDRA SINGH) JUDGE PG Shri Raghuveer Athya vs Shri Param Singh on 12 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89548896/
